claims.text: Equiatomic CoCrFeNiMn can form dynamic precipitates at grain boundaries at approximately 550–600 °C under sufficiently high applied stress.
The grain-boundary dynamic precipitates can be M23C6 or a Cr-rich σ phase.
Thermal aging of CoCrFeNiMn catalysts under catalytic operating conditions, without a specified applied stress, induces these precipitates.
Cr-rich grain-boundary precipitates reduce the accessibility of catalytically active surface sites.
Cr-rich grain-boundary precipitates modify the local electronic structure of the catalyst.
Precipitate-induced site obstruction and electronic modification reduce catalytic activity.
Precipitate formation may alter catalytic selectivity.
The initial CoCrFeNiMn catalyst is a pristine, uniform, single-phase FCC material.
Temperatures around 550–600 °C are known to induce dynamic precipitation in CoCrFeNiMn.
Dynamic precipitation kinetics are active during catalytic operation at approximately 500–600 °C.
Complete phase decomposition can be avoided during the proposed catalytic treatment at 500–600 °C.
Dynamic precipitation lowers the density of available active sites.
A thermally aged catalyst with confirmed precipitates will have a lower turnover frequency than the pristine catalyst under identical reaction conditions.
A thermally aged catalyst with confirmed precipitates will exhibit altered selectivity relative to the pristine catalyst.
The proposed mechanism should apply to CoCrFeNiMn catalysts at 500–600 °C where precipitation is kinetically accessible.
At lower temperatures precipitation is minor.
At very high temperatures complete phase changes could occur.
The magnitude of activity loss and selectivity change depends on precipitate volume fraction and morphology, the catalytic reaction, and the operating environment.

contradictions.description: Selectivity alteration is described as merely possible, but the falsification rule treats the absence of a selectivity shift as sufficient to falsify the hypothesis, even if the predicted activity reduction occurs.
